items.stem: A Vertex AI assistant sometimes invents product details. Which change most directly reduces these fabrications?

options.text: Ground responses in a retrieved, authoritative document set
options.rationale: Correct: grounding supplies real context the model must answer from.
Higher temperature increases randomness and likely more fabrication.
Removing guidance tends to worsen reliability.

options.text: Ask the model to be more confident
options.rationale: Confidence wording does not improve factual accuracy.

items.explanation: Correct: grounding supplies real context the model must answer from.

items.stem: Which TWO controls help keep a tool-using agent safe and predictable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Validate tool-call arguments before executing them
options.rationale: Correct: validation prevents malformed or unsafe calls.

options.text: Cap the number of reasoning/tool steps per request
options.rationale: Correct: a step budget prevents runaway loops and cost.

options.text: Let the agent execute any shell command it proposes
options.rationale: Unrestricted execution is a serious safety risk.

options.text: Hide all errors from the agent
options.rationale: Agents need error signals to recover sensibly.

items.explanation: Correct: both keyed options are right; the distractors are wrong for the reasons given.

options.text: A labelled evaluation set scored against a rubric
options.rationale: Correct: a fixed eval set makes quality comparable across versions.
Marketing does not measure model quality.
One prompt is not a reliable quality measure.
Token limits do not measure quality.
